correctness.rationale: The Hessian determinant factors as 108000 xyz(x+y+z) times four quadratic factors splitting into eight more Hesse reflection lines. I independently symbolically verified that polynomial identity. The sextic is smooth (quadratic form in x³,y³,z³ is nonsingular and coordinate restrictions squarefree); its 72 Hessian intersections are six transverse curve points on each of twelve reflection lines and each is ordinary flex: on x=0, r^6-10r^3+1=0 and F(x,y,ry)=x³[x³-10(1+r³)y³]. The Hessian group takes their tangent directions transitively. Independent projective enumeration over F_211 of the specified dual orbit gives exactly 72 distinct lines and 12 points of multiplicity 6, 216 of 3, and 1728 of 2; weighted pair count is 2556. The supplied exact Z[omega,r] determinant checker explicitly verifies 264 defining zero identities and irreducibility, so finite-field reduction excludes additional characteristic-zero coincidences; a modular count alone would not prove positive characteristic-zero concurrences.
